sub_graphs.title: EIP-6914: Validator Index Reuse State Transitions
sub_graphs.description: Models how validator indices transition from active use through withdrawal to becoming reusable for new deposits

nodes.label: Validator Active
nodes.description: Validator is active with a non-zero balance, performing duties normally

nodes.label: Validator Exited
nodes.description: Validator has exited but has not yet passed the withdrawable epoch

nodes.label: Validator Withdrawable
nodes.description: Validator has reached withdrawable_epoch and can have its balance withdrawn

nodes.label: Validator Withdrawn with Zero Balance
nodes.description: Validator's balance is zero and all funds have been withdrawn

nodes.label: Validator Index Reusable
nodes.description: Validator index is eligible for reassignment: current_epoch > withdrawable_epoch + SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX (65536 epochs ~0.8 years) AND balance == 0

nodes.label: Evaluate is_reusable_validator Predicate
nodes.description: Check if current_epoch > validator.withdrawable_epoch + SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX and validator balance == 0

nodes.label: Get Index for New Validator
nodes.description: Iterate through validator registry to find first reusable index via is_reusable_validator; fallback to appending new index if none found

nodes.label: Validator Index Reassigned to New Deposit
nodes.description: A previously used validator index has been assigned to a new deposit, overwriting the old validator record

edges.label: Validator initiates voluntary exit or is slashed
Both conditions met: epoch exceeded AND balance == 0
Reusable index found and assigned to new deposit

external_entities.name: New Validator Depositor
external_entities.description: External entity submitting a new 32 ETH deposit that may be assigned a reused validator index

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6914: Validator Reusability Validation Rules
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation checks that determine whether a validator index can safely be reused

nodes.label: Candidate Validator Index for Reuse
nodes.description: A validator index is being evaluated as a potential candidate for reuse during deposit processing

nodes.label: Check Balance is Zero
nodes.description: Verify that the validator's balance in BeaconState.balances is exactly zero

nodes.label: Index Eligible for Reuse
nodes.description: Both time-lock and balance checks passed; index can be reused

nodes.label: Index Not Eligible for Reuse
nodes.description: One or both checks failed; index cannot be reused yet

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6914: Security Implications of Validator Index Reuse
sub_graphs.description: Models security boundaries around validator index reuse including potential confusion attacks and the time-lock safety mechanism

nodes.label: Old Validator Record Exists
nodes.description: Historical validator record with old pubkey, withdrawal credentials, and historical duties exists at an index

nodes.label: Overwrite Validator Record with New Deposit
nodes.description: Replace the old validator record at a reused index with new deposit data (new pubkey, withdrawal credentials)

nodes.label: Validator Index Identity Changed
nodes.description: The validator index now maps to a completely different identity (pubkey/withdrawal credentials) than it historically did

nodes.label: Enforce SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX Time-Lock
nodes.description: Wait 65536 epochs (~0.8 years) after withdrawable_epoch to ensure all historical references to this index have finalized and any slashing evidence has been processed

edges.label: New pubkey and withdrawal credentials assigned to index

external_entities.name: Historical Index References
external_entities.description: External systems, explorers, or applications that may reference validator indices by number and could be confused by identity changes

ambiguities.text: The spec does not specify what happens to historical attestation/proposal records when a validator index is reused.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume historical records remain associated with the index but are understood to belong to the previous validator identity. Applications must track pubkey changes.

ambiguities.text: The iteration order in get_index_for_new_validator returns the 'first' reusable index, but does not specify if this has deterministic ordering implications across clients.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume iteration is over the validator registry in index order (0, 1, 2, ...) which is deterministic since BeaconState.validators is an ordered list.

implicit_assumptions.description: The SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX value of 65536 epochs (~0.8 years) is assumed to be sufficient for all pending slashing evidence to be included and all historical references to be considered stale.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If slashing evidence for the old validator emerges after index reuse, the new validator at that index could be incorrectly penalized or the slashing evidence could be unprovable.

implicit_assumptions.description: External systems (block explorers, staking dashboards, indexers) are assumed to handle validator identity changes at reused indices correctly.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users could confuse old and new validators at the same index, leading to incorrect balance tracking, false slashing reports, or social engineering attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The balance withdrawal mechanism is assumed to always eventually bring the balance to exactly zero for fully exited validators.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If dust balances remain, validator indices could never become reusable, defeating the purpose of the EIP.
